newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends limit-down on panic selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends limit-down on panic selling.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly limit-down on Tuesday on panic selling triggered by overnight heavy losses on the London Metal Exchange, after sharp gains in the past week, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended limit-down at 20,440 yuan ($2,462) per tonne, losing 640 yuan. It opened at 20,600 and hit an intra-day high of 20,650.
December fell 640 to 20,130, January 630 to 20,440, February 650 to 20,430, April 630 to 20,420, May 600 to 20,410 and June 630 to 20,670.
Combined volume rose to 85,620 tonnes from 50,990.
